ongunhae--huangdi.scene: INTRODUCING ON GUNHAE, Chunchu's attendant — the same height as his master, which will matter. Dawn at sea on the voyage home from Chang'an, on the deck of a Silla ship. Low three-quarter angle from the deck boards: he kneels close beside his master (only an out-of-focus magenta silk sleeve at the frame edge) and leans in, head half-turned toward the horizon, saying low and urgent: "My lord. The small boat." A calm, loyal, steady face — stubbled jaw set, eyes narrowed at the threat, no panic; beside his knee on the deck lies a folded great-coat of Tang brocade. Behind him: a grey-green swell, wind-torn spray, taut hemp rigging and a weathered wooden mast, and on the horizon the small dark square sail of an ancient wooden oared boat closing in (7th-century wooden boats only — no modern ships, no metal hulls). The low sunrise breaks through storm cloud and rakes across his face from the side in hard amber-brown light (#8a6240).

jukji--royal-secretariat.scene: INTRODUCING KIM JUKJI, the Hwarang who sailed with Chunchu to Chang'an and wrote down everything — quiet, exact, always holding the right paper. Late morning in a narrow side hall of the Silla palace in Seorabeol, the day the Royal Secretariat is born. Low three-quarter angle across a crowded low desk: he sits on his heels, leaning forward, pressing a seal down onto a petition with one hand while the other already holds out a tied scroll to a courier (only out-of-focus hands in a plain Silla hanbok sleeve at the frame edge), glancing up with a quick, dry, confident half-smile: "Petition. Seal. Courier." Behind him, painted loosely in dusty sunlight: shelves of tied bamboo scrolls, plain undecorated timber walls with no hangings, drifting dust motes, and through a far doorway the blurred shapes of old council lords still debating. All paper is blank — no calligraphy, characters or writing anywhere in the frame. A hard shaft of daylight through a lattice window rakes across his face and the desk, tinting the dust soft jade green (#6a9e7a).

gaozong-emperor--jiabeng.scene: INTRODUCING THE THIRD EMPEROR OF TANG, the heir who rises from his father's deathbed as emperor. Night in the Cuiwei Palace in the mountains, the hour the old emperor dies. Low three-quarter angle from the floor: he is rising from his knees, both hands lifting the imperial jade seal wrapped in yellow silk — the moment he takes the throne. His eyes are red-rimmed and wet, jaw clenched, grief held back by force, lips parting on his first words as emperor: "From this day… We will listen." Behind him, painted in drifting incense smoke and blue-green shadow: a tall Tang hall of vermilion pillars and white lattice, rows of kneeling officials in dark Tang court robes and black caps dissolving into the haze, dozens of candle flames as warm bokeh. A tall bronze candle-tree beside him throws hard gold-tan light (#b8935a) up across his face and the yellow silk.

chunchu-king--king-muyeol.scene: INTRODUCING KING MUYEOL — Kim Chunchu, the morning the Harmony Council makes him king of Silla. The council hall in Seorabeol. Low three-quarter angle, a slightly wider shot framed from the knees up: the whole crown sits well below the top edge, with a dark band of hall ceiling and roof beams above it. Crowned in Silla gold, he lowers himself into the throne for the first time, one hand on the carved armrest, the other smoothing the dragon-embroidered robe over his knee, head tilted with an amused, half-lidded, knowing smile — a handsome man who is good at talk and laughter, murmuring that nobody could find a reason to object (spoken, never written: no subtitles, no captions). Behind him, painted in morning haze and incense smoke: dark red timber pillars, a painted screen, and the bowed backs of council lords in Silla court robes as soft out-of-focus shapes. A low shaft of morning sun through the open doors rakes across his face, the gold spangles of the crown and the silk, warmed with magenta (#D8258C).

munhee-queen--king-muyeol.scene: INTRODUCING QUEEN MUNMYUNG — Munhee, who married in disgrace and now stands beside the throne. Morning in the council hall in Seorabeol, the day her husband is made king. Low three-quarter angle, framed from the waist up with the whole crown well inside the frame and dark roof beams above it: she stands beside the throne (the king is only an out-of-focus red-and-gold sleeve on the armrest at the frame edge) while a court lady's hands (out of focus, in Silla hanbok sleeves) settle the Silla gold crown onto her coiled braids — the moment she becomes queen. She glances sideways at the camera, chin up, one eyebrow raised, a delighted, wicked, satisfied smile, as if remarking that the sister who sold her the dream for one silk skirt undercharged (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind her, painted in morning haze and incense smoke: red timber pillars, gold-trimmed hangings, lantern bokeh. A shaft of morning sun through the hall doors rakes across her face, the gold of the crown and the embroidered silk in warm rose-pink light (#E07FA8).

jayi--jahee.scene: INTRODUCING JAHEE, a harbour girl who counts faster than the customs men. Late afternoon in her father's counting room at Danghang harbour on Silla's west coast. Low three-quarter angle across a low desk heaped with bamboo tally sticks and rolled ledgers: she leans in on one elbow, tapping a tally stick with her father's fine brush, looking up and sideways at the prince off-frame (only an out-of-focus Silla silk sleeve at the frame edge) with one eyebrow raised and a cool, unimpressed, faintly amused face: "Your sums are wrong." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind her, through a wide open door, painted loosely in sea haze: grain ships at the quay, tall masts and furled sails, gulls, the glitter of the incoming tide as warm bokeh. The low sun off the water rakes across her face and lilac silk from the side in soft rose-pink light (#e8a0bf).

hyukgose--hyukgose.scene: INTRODUCING HYUKGOSE, born from an egg and crowned king before his voice broke. A bright spring morning on a hilltop above the Alcheon river, the day the six village chiefs make him king. He is a BOY of thirteen — a younger, beardless version of the face on the sheet. Low worm's-eye angle, framed from the waist up with the whole crown and the chiefs' hands well inside the frame: he kneels upright on a straw mat as old chiefs' weathered hands (out of focus, in plain undyed hemp sleeves) lower a gold crown with tree-shaped uprights onto his head; it is a little too big and tilts over one brow. He gazes up past the camera, solemn and clear-eyed, chin up, trying very hard to look like a king, one corner of his mouth almost smiling. Behind him a vast bright sky of towering sunlit clouds, a wheeling flock of cranes and swallows, green hills and the glittering river far below. The low morning sun rakes across his face in clean bright blue-gold light (#6f9fe8).

alyoung--hyukgose.scene: INTRODUCING LADY ALYOUNG, born from a dragon's rib — the one person in Surabol who can tell the king no. Early morning at Alyeong well in a grove outside Surabol. She is not queen yet: NO crown — her hair exactly as on the sheet, the high knot and its gold pin. Low three-quarter angle: a young woman kneels on the packed earth at the stone rim of the old well, sleeves pushed back, a wooden dipper in her wet hands, and turns her head toward someone off-frame with a cool, level, faintly amused gaze, one eyebrow lifting, as if about to ask: "Who measures the virtue?" (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind her, painted loosely in morning mist: the moss-dark stone rim of the well, willow and pine, sunlit haze, and high in the pale gold sky the long serpentine coils of a cloud shaped like a departing dragon. A low sunrise shaft through the trees rakes across her face and blue silk from the side in soft pale-blue light (#a8c8f0), droplets on her fingers catching it.

talhae--talhae.scene: INTRODUCING SEOK TALHAE, who arrived in a chest and talks like he owns the beach. Afternoon in King Suro's timber hall in Golden Gaya; he has just walked in off the sand. HE IS: a very tall, long-limbed, sea-weathered young man, deeply tanned, clean-shaven, sly narrow eyes and a broad easy grin, black hair in a loose topknot with salt-stiff strands falling free; plain undyed hemp jeogori and trousers, sleeves rolled, a fisherman's cord belt, still damp with sea water. Low worm's-eye angle: he leans one shoulder against a timber pillar, arms folded, chin tipped toward the throne (King Suro only a dark out-of-focus shape in purple robes at the frame edge), perfectly polite and utterly shameless: "I've come for your throne." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him the hall's open doors blaze with bright sea glare, sunlit sand and surf as soft bokeh; the afternoon sun rakes across his face in hard sea-blue and gold light (#5a7fa8).

yuridora--exile.scene: INTRODUCING YURI DORA, king of Tamla, who tells stories to men nobody else will talk to. Bright morning on a black volcanic beach on Tamla. Low three-quarter angle from the sand: he squats on his heels beside a half-drowned castaway (only an out-of-focus shoulder and tangled black hair at the frame edge, in torn Baekje hanbok), forearms on his knees, a gourd of water dangling from one hand, grinning down with wry, unhurried amusement, eyebrows up: "Ah. Not one for greetings, then." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, painted in loose sunlit strokes: black basalt boulders, white surf, a wide bright blue sky with tall clouds, the green cone of a volcano far off, and a basket of bright tangerines on the rocks as a warm accent. The hard morning sun rakes across his face, moustache and orange robe from the side in warm tangerine light (#ff9a3d).

heavenearthking--heaven-earth-king.scene: INTRODUCING HEAVEN–EARTH KING, the god with two jobs and one desk, who dreams about breakfast. Night in his office above the clouds, in the time of two suns and two moons. Low three-quarter angle across a huge desk buried in stacks of closed, tied ledgers and rolled scrolls (no open pages, no writing anywhere): he has just jerked awake from a nap on his folded arms, hair a little mussed, sitting up slowly, one hand on his belly and the other touching his lips, eyes wide, a slow astonished grin spreading across his clean unmarked face: "…Huh. One each." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, through a tall open lattice window, a vast night sky of moonlit cloud with TWO full moons hanging side by side, silver-blue cloud banks drifting below them. An ancient open-flame oil lamp — a small bronze dish with a bare wick, no glass — on the desk throws hard crimson light (#C30000) up across his face and his half-white, half-black-and-red robe, while cold blue moonlight (#3E79E4) edges his far shoulder.

sumyeongjangja--heaven-earth-king.scene: INTRODUCING SUMYUNG JANGJA, the richest man under two suns, who lends one measure and collects two. A white-hot afternoon in the time of two suns, at the door of one of his nine storehouses. Low worm's-eye angle: he stands in the storehouse doorway, half-turned away, scooping rice into a square wooden measure with his back to the borrower, looking down his nose at her over his shoulder (only a poor young woman's out-of-focus hands holding out an empty gourd bowl at the frame edge, in a patched Korean hemp sleeve), half-lidded, blank, contemptuous, mouth turned down: "One measure. Two when you pay it back." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, painted in shimmering heat haze: a row of tiled storehouse roofs, a tethered horse and a crouching dog as soft dark shapes, and a bleached sky with TWO blazing suns. The doubled sunlight rakes across his face and white robe from the side, throwing two hard shadows, the olive-gold collar catching it (#8a7a3a).

daebyeol-young--heaven-earth-king.scene: INTRODUCING BIG STAR, the elder twin, who would rather be right than first. Dusk outside his mother's poor thatched house, in the time of two suns and two moons. He is a CHILD of twelve, small and skinny: a smooth, round, boyish webtoon face with soft cheeks and NO facial hair at all — no moustache, no goatee, no stubble. The sheet shows him as a grown man; take only the eye shape, brows and short messy dark hair from it and draw him as the twelve-year-old boy he is now. A poor child's version of the sheet's clothes: a worn, patched black hemp jeogori with a faded blue collar band, sleeves too long for his thin wrists, a small child's wooden bow propped beside him. Low three-quarter angle: he sits on the worn wooden doorstep with his bony knees up and an elbow on one knee, turning his head toward his younger brother off-frame with a calm, quiet, older-brother look, low and steady: "Leave it. Mom's tired." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, painted in loose dusk strokes: a dirt yard, a crooked brushwood fence, a gourd vine on the eaves, and a deep blue sky with TWO small setting suns side by side on the horizon while two pale moons rise above. The last low sunlight rakes across his face from the side, the shadows pooling in cool deep blue (#3B6FBF).

sobyeol-young--heaven-earth-king.scene: INTRODUCING LITTLE STAR, the younger twin, who would rather be first. Dusk in the dirt yard of his mother's poor thatched house, in the time of two suns and two moons. He is a BOY of about twelve — the sheet is a photo of him grown up: redraw it as a boyish, beardless webtoon face in clean ink line (same eyes, brows and red-streaked dark hair; NO beard). A poor child's version of the sheet's clothes: a worn, dusty white hemp jeogori with a plain red collar band and a red tie. Low worm's-eye angle: he has just stormed in through the brushwood gate, dusty, a scrape on one cheek, fists clenched, leaning forward and jabbing a thumb back over his shoulder at the village, loud and indignant, mouth wide mid-complaint: "Mom. Who's our father. The other kids are at it again." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, painted in loose dusk strokes: the crooked fence, a gourd vine, a few tiny jeering village children far off as dark shapes, and a burning orange sky where two suns sink while two pale moons rise. The hot low sunlight rakes across his face from the side in fierce red (#C94040).

sulmun--sulmun.scene: INTRODUCING GRANDMOTHER SULMUN, the Great Lady who made the island — the sea comes to her knee, and she has opinions about the view. Morning at the dawn of the world, at the shore of the newborn island of Tamla. She is enormous: low worm's-eye angle from the waves far below, looking up at her from the waist up as she stands in the sea, holding her red apron-skirt bunched up full of dark seabed earth and stones, a thin stream of earth trickling down through a hole in it. She tilts her head and squints critically at the view, one brow raised, lips pursed in an amused, opinionated half-smile. Clouds drift past her shoulders; tiny seabirds wheel round her like gnats. Behind her a vast bright morning sky of towering cumulus, and the half-built cone of a mountain rising from the sea beside her. The low morning sun rakes across her face and white jeogori from the side, sea mist tinting the shadows soft grey-green (#7f9c8b).

baekjuto--three-princes.scene: INTRODUCING BAEKJUTO, a farming goddess who crossed the sea to find a husband — and is about to find one. A windy late afternoon on a half-ploughed field of black volcanic soil on the island. Low three-quarter angle from the furrow, a slightly wider shot framed from the knees up so the whole tall coiled hairdo and its amethyst ornaments sit well below the top edge, with open sky above them; she is painted into the field in the same light, with no white outline around her silhouette. She stands over an abandoned plough with its empty wooden yoke and dangling harness — no ox anywhere — holding up the cut rope in one hand, the other on her hip, staring off-frame at her husband with wide, outraged, disbelieving eyes and an open mouth: "You ate the ox. The one I gave you to plough with. The whole ox?" (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind her, painted in loose windblown strokes: dark furrows, a thin column of cookfire smoke drifting from the field's edge, a bright blue sky with racing clouds, and the long slope of a volcano in the distance. The low gold sun rakes across her face, her amethyst hair ornaments and violet silk (#c084fc).

socheonguk--three-princes.scene: INTRODUCING SOCHEON-GUK, the hunt god with a big appetite — bigger than you're thinking. Dusk at the edge of a ploughed field on the island. Low three-quarter angle: he sits on a log by a roaring cookfire, a huge roasted rib bone in one fist, a heap of gnawed ox bones and TWO ox skulls at his feet, cheeks full, grease in his beard, looking up at his wife off-frame with a guilty, sheepish, still-chewing grin, eyebrows raised: "…I also ate someone else's." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). His bow leans against the log. Behind him, painted in loose smoky strokes: drifting woodsmoke and sparks, the dark furrows of the field, a lone abandoned plough, and a warm violet-orange dusk sky. The cookfire below him throws hard amber light (#a16207) up across his face, fur collar and grinning teeth.

sanbangdeok--stone-lady.scene: INTRODUCING SANBANGDUK, a goddess who stepped out of the Sanbang cliff to see the world — and the world noticed. A misty morning at the spring at the foot of Sanbang mountain, a sheer cliff of grey volcanic rock above the sea. Her face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: long loose wavy black hair, small drop earrings, a pale sea-green jeogori under the sheet's grey stone-textured shawl. Close low three-quarter angle: sitting on a mossy stone at the spring's edge, she holds a poor young man's rough hand in both of hers (only his out-of-focus hand and plain undyed hemp sleeve at the frame edge) and looks up at him through her lashes with shy, astonished tenderness, lips parted: "When I hold your hand I don't feel like stone." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind her, painted in drifting sea mist: the towering grey cliff with a dark cave mouth, ferns and dripping moss, the spring pool catching light, the bright sea beyond. A shaft of morning sun breaks through the mist and rakes across her face and silk from the side, the cool mist around her tinted sea-green (#8fb3a8).

sara--gardener.scene: INTRODUCING HALLAKGUNGI, born a servant in a rich man's house — and he means to find his father. Night, the hour he leaves for the far west. He is a YOUTH of about fifteen: his face redrawn from the photo-like sheet as a younger, beardless webtoon face in clean ink line, keeping its likeness (eyes, brows, short dark hair over the brow), in the sheet's plain dark green hemp robe, a small cloth bundle on a strap across his chest. Low three-quarter angle at the back gate of the rich man's compound: half-turned in mid-stride, he looks back one last time toward his mother's doorway, where an open clay oil-dish lamp burns warm and out of focus; his face set hard, jaw tight, eyes wet but unflinching. Behind him, in loose moonlit strokes: a tiled wall and a plank gate, a dark bamboo grove swaying, a dirt road running west under a huge low moon in a cloud-streaked indigo sky. Cold moonlight, filtered leaf-green (#8FBF8A) through the bamboo, rakes across his face from the side.

jacheongbi--gardener.scene: INTRODUCING JACHEONGBI — disguise, scholarship, and not one ounce of patience. Night in a lamp-lit study hall where women are not allowed; she has cut her hair and come dressed as a boy. Her face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness — but NOT the sheet's long hair or grain ornaments: her hair is cropped short and tied up in a boy's small topknot with a plain cloth band, a plain pale scholar's robe over her pink jeogori. Low three-quarter angle across a low reading desk: she has already finished her passage, brush laid down, chin propped on one fist, and slides a sidelong, exasperated, smug glance at the slow boy beside her (only an out-of-focus pale-blue sleeve at the frame edge), lips pressed on a barely hidden smirk. Behind her, painted in warm lamp haze: paper lattice doors, closed bundles of bamboo-slip books and tied scrolls (no writing anywhere), rain streaking the dark courtyard beyond as soft bokeh. An open clay oil-dish lamp with a bare flame on the desk lights her face from below in hard warm pink light (#e879a6).

mundoryeong--gardener.scene: INTRODUCING MUN DORYEONG, a boy from the sky sent down to study — very good at books, very bad at noticing things. Night at the parting stream, the last night of three years at the same desk. His face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: a young man, loose black strands, a topknot tied with the pale blue ribbon, white robe with a pale blue collar — none of the sheet's sparkles. Low three-quarter angle from the water's edge: he crouches on the flat stones of the bank, fully dressed, sleeves rolled, wet hands frozen halfway to his face, and stares upstream at someone off-frame, stunned — eyes wide, ears and cheeks flushing red, mouth falling open as it finally dawns on him: "…I had no eyes." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, painted in loose moonlit strokes: a rushing stream silvered by moonlight, willow branches, drifting mist and fireflies as soft bokeh, a starry indigo sky. The cold moonlight rakes across his face and white robe from the side in clear sky-blue light (#7dd3fc), water drops glittering on his fingers.

yumla--kangrim.scene: INTRODUCING YUMLA, the judge of the dead — every ledger in the dark ends on his desk. The gate of the underworld, at the end of the road down. His face redrawn from the photo-like sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: grey hair under the small ornate silver topknot crown, full grey beard, heavy carved-bead necklace over a black robe with deep purple under-layers. Low worm's-eye angle across his great judgment desk stacked with closed ledgers and tied scrolls (no writing anywhere): he sits enthroned, leaning forward on folded hands, looking down at the living official who has dared to summon him (only an out-of-focus shoulder and the black brim of a gat at the frame edge), heavy-lidded, utterly unimpressed, a judge who has already decided: "Go home. I will come at the hour I name." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, in drifting grey fog: the colossal dark timbers of the underworld gate under a heavy giwa-tiled roof, its lintel bare, low iron fire baskets on tripods fading into the mist, a long procession of tiny pale souls walking down a road into the haze. On the desk a flat, shallow bronze dish lamp — a plain saucer of oil with one small bright flame on a bare wick, no handle, no spout, no glass — lights his face, beard and beads from below in hard violet light (#7c3aed).

chunbok--coup.scene: INTRODUCING SATEK CHUNBOK, the young Satek in the Satek chair, sitting for the king. Morning in the Assembly hall at Sabi, the day the king fires the whole Assembly. Low three-quarter angle: he lowers himself into the Premier's carved wooden chair at the head of the hall, hands settling on the armrests, back straight, a careful, composed, procedural face, his eyes turned hard sideways (not at the camera) toward his own clan watching him — only blurred dark shapes of Baekje nobles along the wall. On his head, high over the topknot, the Baekje great-clan gilt-bronze cap — NOT a European crown, no ring of points around the brow: a tall narrow pointed cap shaped like a peaked hood, all of pierced gold-bronze openwork, a broad engraved band across the brow, a curved openwork crest arching over the top, two small cup-shaped finials on thin stems rising at the back, a flat leaf-plume at the front. The sheet's red-and-gold court robe. Behind him, in morning haze and incense smoke: plain unmarked dark red timber pillars (no plaques, no hanging boards, no calligraphy anywhere), tall paper-lattice doors, a bronze incense burner trailing smoke. A hard shaft of morning sun through the lattice rakes across his face, the gilt cap and the red silk in warm gold (#d4a94e).

yuri-prince--onjo.scene: INTRODUCING YURI, a boy from Buyeo with bad aim or bad luck, and a mother who will not answer one question. A bright afternoon in a village lane in Buyeo, near the well. He is a lanky teenage boy of about fifteen and not a king yet: NO crown, no gold — his orange head-cloth and the orange cloth mask over his nose and mouth exactly as on the sheet, the red robe with the dark collar, a plain wooden staff slung across his back. Low worm's-eye angle: he has just loosed a shot from his leather sling — the empty sling dangles loose from his raised fingers, the pebble long gone — and he freezes mid-follow-through, eyes huge and guilty, brows shot UP in an oops (not angry, not frowning), as far off at the frame edge the clay water jar on a woman's shoulder bursts into water and shards (only her blurred back and shoulder in a plain Buyeo hemp jeogori). Behind him, painted loosely: thatched roofs, a tall pine, sparrows scattering into a bright blue sky with drifting clouds. The hard afternoon sun rakes across his eyes and red robe from the side, warm coral light (#e07a5f) in the flying droplets.

heungsu--heungsu.scene: INTRODUCING HEUNGSU, a Baekje minister sent far from court for saying what the king didn't want to hear. Late afternoon at a river berth on Satek water, the day the clans put Gyebek on a boat; he is the only man from court who came down to the dock. His face redrawn from the painted sheet in clean webtoon ink line, keeping its likeness: a tired, lined face, moustache and stubble, black topknot with a gold band, the gold-ochre silk court robe over a white collar. Low three-quarter angle from the dock planks: unarmed, he leans forward with one hand half-raised toward the departing man (only an out-of-focus dark shoulder with a crimson scarf at the frame edge), caught between disbelief and dread, brows drawn, mouth just opening: "You… you truly mean to go? Without a word to the king—" (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, in loose golden river haze: a low, open, mastless wooden boat with long oars at the berth, reeds, the wide river and far bluffs dissolving in mist, gulls. The low afternoon sun rakes across his face and robe from the side in hard old-gold light (#b98f33).

sudingfang--yellow-mountain.scene: INTRODUCING THE RED FOWL (his nickname) — Su Dingfang, Tang's great general, sixty-five, who still prefers to march at night. Night in a blizzard on the open steppe, the night he took a qaghan's camp before anyone in it found their boots. The face as on the sheet, aged to sixty-five: weathered skin, a grey-streaked topknot held by a long pin, a grey-streaked beard. Low worm's-eye angle: he rides a dark steppe horse at the head of a column, in black Tang lamellar armour and a red war-cloak, a long Tang halberd held upright in one fist and no sword, turning in the saddle to look back at his men with a flat, dry, unhurried face, snow clinging to his brows: "Snow is just cold sand. Nobody expects you in it." (spoken, never written: no subtitles). Behind him, in loose driving snow: muffled riders dissolving into the white dark, plain unmarked red pennants snapping in the wind, and far ahead the small orange fires of a sleeping camp of round felt tents as bokeh. A torch carried beside him throws hard red-orange light (#d95f4b) across his face and armour from the side.
